standard_prerequisites.name: A map out of a perfect complex into a bounded below complex of quasi-coherent modules vanishes in low degrees, so condition (2) follows from boundedness below

The Hom groups of the derived category, the Ext groups and the derived Hom, as well as the dual of a perfect complex and the global sections of the derived tensor product, are related by the standard identifications
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that conditions (2) to (6) are all equivalent.

standard_prerequisites.name: A perfect complex generating the derived category is a classical generator, and a property of objects that is inherited by direct sums, summands and shifts and satisfies the two out of three property holds for all perfect complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Extends the equivalent conditions from the given generator to every perfect object, giving condition (7).

standard_prerequisites.name: The induction principle on quasi-compact opens reduces a statement about all quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes to the affine case and a union step
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the converse to the affine case and the union of two opens.

core_obligations: Show that (1) implies (2): shifting the argument turns the vanishing into the vanishing of Hom from the generator into a bounded below complex in low degrees, which is the cited statement (proof lines 10859-10862).

Record that (2), (3), (4) are equivalent by the identifications between Hom, Ext and derived Hom, and that (5), (6) are equivalent because cohomology is the cohomology of the derived global sections; then use duality of the perfect generator to see that the two blocks are equivalent (proof lines 10863-10872).

Note that (7) implies (2) trivially, and conversely use that the generator is a classical generator: the property of having the derived Hom bounded below is inherited by direct sums, summands and shifts and satisfies the two out of three property, so the cited criterion extends it to all perfect complexes; the same applies to the other properties (proof lines 10873-10886).

Prove that the equivalent conditions imply (1) by induction on quasi-compact opens, starting with the affine case: for the structure sheaf as the test object, condition (7) gives the vanishing of the cohomology in low degrees, and on an affine scheme the complex is determined by its derived global sections, so it is bounded below (proof lines 10887-10894).

For the union step assume the implication known on the two opens and their intersection, take a perfect complex whose restriction to one open generates, and build from a Koszul complex on equations cutting the complement of that open a perfect complex supported on the closed complement and isomorphic to the Koszul complex on the other open (proof lines 10895-10915).

Use the second description of that complex to see the vanishing of Hom from the Koszul complex into the restricted complex in low degrees, apply the orthogonal statement to obtain a truncation isomorphism with the direct image from the intersection, deduce the vanishing on the first open, apply the induction hypothesis there, and conclude boundedness below on the whole scheme using that direct image preserves bounded below objects (proof lines 10916-10950).
proof_roadmap: The implications among (1) to (6) by the standard Hom and dual identifications (proof lines 10859-10872).
Extension from the generator to all perfect complexes by the classical generator argument (proof lines 10873-10886).
The affine case of the converse via the structure sheaf and the comparison statement (proof lines 10887-10894).
The union step: construct the auxiliary perfect complex, truncate using the orthogonal statement, and conclude by induction (proof lines 10895-10950).
